author: Mark Atwood
text:
Entangled with the .2/.3/.4/.10 architectural decision family (typed methods on ChatBackend vs apply_space_patch variants vs may_* hook). .9 is the read-side sibling of .3 (SpaceInvite manage_members enforcement on create): whichever architecture lands for write-side permission gating presumably also shapes how visibility-scoped reads work. Options:

(A) Typed read methods on ChatBackend: `list_visible_invites_in_space(caller, account_id, space_id)`, `list_visible_bans_in_space`. Handler calls the typed method instead of the generic `get_objects::<SpaceInvite>`. Backend resolves caller's effective permissions in the Space and returns the spec-allowed subset.

(B) Generic `get_objects::<T>` learns to filter by caller per spec rules. Backend looks at type-erased `O::TYPE_NAME` and applies the right filter. Type-erasure inside the backend is messy (per the .3 comment).

(C) Handler-side post-filter using a new `ChatBackend::member_effective_permissions(caller, account_id, space_id)` read helper + `principal_id(caller)`. Handler does the projection. Workspace AGENTS.md says backend is canonical for permission enforcement, so the backend must still re-verify; in get's case this means the get path itself must scope, not just trust the handler.

Recommendation: Path A. Same recommendation as .3/.4, consistent with the typed-methods-for-spec-mandated-semantics shape. Adds 2 trait methods (list_visible_invites_in_space, list_visible_bans_in_space) with default impls returning forbidden so backends fail closed. Handler changes are mechanical.

Also requires the same treatment for /changes and /queryChanges on SpaceInvite and SpaceBan (id lists must be post-filtered too, otherwise rate of new invites leaks). That's 4 more typed list methods (changes + queryChanges for each) OR the changes-log gets a per-type visibility filter inside the backend.

Adding dependency on JMAP-x2gd.3 so .9 stays off the ready frontier until the architectural decision lands. Not labeling .9 as human — the human decision lives on .3, not duplicated here.
